newsitem.title: USA: Lot carried record annual cargo in '96.
newsitem.headline: Lot carried record annual cargo in '96.

text.p: LOT Polish Airlines announced 1996 as its fifth consecutive year of increased cargo traffic, setting a record for tonnes it carried in one year.
The carrier said it transported 20,634 tonnes of cargo in 1996, a 16 percent increase against 17,819 tonnes it moved the previous year.

"The record growth can be attributed to the added number of flights we've been offering between North America and Poland over the past few years, and the development of the emerging markets beyond our borders," said Margaret Budnicka, North American Sales Manager at John F. Kennedy Airport.

The state-owned carrier said its North American operations carried 6,247 tonnes of cargo between the U.S. and Poland in 1996, against 5,555 tonnes in 1995, a 12.5 percent increase. It said Chicago's O'Hare and JFK airports were the two biggest international gateways for cargo uplift.
The carrier increased its peak-season service between the U.S. and Poland to 26 flights per week from its 20 flights per week in both 1995 and 1996.
Up to a 60 percent decrease in cargo costs will be extended as part of its summer season, beginning May 1, it said. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
